Veeru vs Parvatibai on 5 December, 2025
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On The 5 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 9194 of 2024
 Veeru
 Versus
 Parvatibai And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Sameer Verma, learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri Arun Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the res  Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent [
 ORDER

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 04.11.2024 passed in claim case Nos.2491/2022 and 2752/2022 whereby challenging the apportionment done by the claims tribunal of the compensation between the husband and mother of the deceased.
2. The facts of case are that on 30.06.2022 deceased Pinki was going along with her friend Rajkumar and Parvatibai on Activa scooter towards Pardeshipura.
Rajkumar was riding Activa and both were sitting as pillion riders.

When they reached near Chandragupta Mourya square, respondent No.2 came driving container bearing registration number UP78-HN-2004 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into Activa scooter because of which Pinki, Rajkumar and Parvatibai sustained grievous injuries and all of them 2 MA-9194-2024 were rushed to MY Hospital where Pinki died during treatment.
The incident was reported to police station-Heera Nagar, Indore.

3 . Due to death of Pinki, two separate claim petitions came to be filed in terms of Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
one by husband of Pinki and other by mother.
The claims tribunal heard both the claim petitions together and after recording evidence held that the cause of accident was rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle.

Thus, while allowing both the petitions, total compensation of Rs.19,60,672/-
was awarded and out of which an amount of Rs.9,80,336/- was awarded to the husband-Veeru and equal amount was awarded to Parvatibai, this apportionment is under challenge in the present appeal.

4. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that in fact the claim petition filed by Parvatibai was not be entertained by the claims tribunal in view of the settled position of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Deepshikha and another Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd.
and others in SLP 22265/2018 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that once daughter is married, logical presumption is that she now has rights on matrimonial households and also financially supported by her husband or his family unless proven otherwise.

He submits that in the present case mother of the deceased Parvatibai has not proven otherwise i.e. to say although she initially pleaded that there was a dispute Veeru vs Parvatibai on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41774054/
1 between deceased Pinki and her husband Veeru, however, in her cross examination she yielded to the questions of counsel for Veeru and had admitted that there were no strained relations between the two and had there been no accident, Veeru would have taken her daughter Pinki 3 MA-9194-2024 to her matrimonial home.

He thus submits that mother of the deceased is not entitled for any compensation, hence, prays for dismissal of claim petition of mother Parvatibai and payment of entire awarded amount to Veeru-appellant.

5. Controverting the same, learned counsel for the mother- Parvatibai submits that it has clearly been pleaded by the mother of the deceased that after only about 1 and 1/2 month there was a dispute between the husband and wife i.e. the deceased and Veeru-the appellant.
That is why she returned to her maternal home and was living with her mother.
He also points out that the mother of the deceased is a widow who was totally dependent on the income of her daughter.

He also points out that in the same accident the mother had also suffered grievous injuries, which has rendered her totally incapable in doing any job, thus, she is now dependent on the amount of compensation which has been awarded by the claims tribunal.

He further submits that in view of the clear findings recorded by the claims tribunal in para 25, the mother was able to prove that she was dependent on the income of her daughter - Pinki as such he supports the findings of the award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that this is not the dispute to which the insurance company is concerned.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

From perusal of the pleadings in the claim petition filed by the mother of the deceased though it is seen that she has pleaded that there was strain relations between the husband-wife i.e. the appellant Veeru and deceased Pinki and her daughter was living with her, however, extended cross 4 MA-9194-2024 examination of Parvatibai has yielded completely different story.

She has not only admitted that the relations between the two were cordial but has also admitted that even the funeral expenses were borne by husband and after accident she was taken care of by the husband.
As such, it appears that there were no strained relations as is evident from the cross-examination of Parvatibai herself between deceased-Pinki and husband-Veeru.

However, considering the peculiar facts of the present case that the mother of the deceased-Pinki is all alone in the whole world as her husband had already died and there is no issue other than deceased Pinki.
As such, the Court is not inclined to hold that the mother of the deceased was not at all dependent on her income.
However, in the peculiar facts of the present case the apportionment done by the claims tribunal appears to be somewhat disproportionate.

Considering the same, the award is hereby modified to the extent that out of total compensation awarded by the claims tribunal i.e. to the tune of Rs.19,60,672/-, 65% of the same is to be paid to the appellant and 35% is to be paid to the respondent No.1/mother of the deceased.
9.
Learned counsel for the respective parties have informed this Court that in view of the pending dispute in the present appeal, no amount has been disbursed to any of the claimant.

As such, the Registry is directed to immediately return the record of the claims tribunal to the concerned claims Veeru vs Parvatibai on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41774054/
2 tribunal so as to enable the claims tribunal to immediately disburse the amount to the respective claimants in the ratio as directed herein above.

10. This apportionment is done looking to the peculiar circumstances of the present case i.e.
respondent No.1/Parvatibai is all alone in the world and 5 MA-9194-2024 also the fact that the deceased daughter was travelling at the time of accident with her mother.
11.
Apart from the above question of apportionment, no other point was argued by the learned counsel for the appellant.
12. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
